answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 61 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The echo graph is validated at intake and the juniper frontier is published, and therefore the ancestry of every answer is public, and delta anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Every submission must name 4 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight.
